name: Illegalism
summary: Illegalism is a current of individualist anarchism, mainly French and Italian around 1880-1914, that treated crime as a form of revolt. Its adherents held that theft (individual reclamation), burglary, forgery and violence against the bourgeoisie were legitimate ways to live free of wage labor and to provoke revolution at once. They rejected the state, law, property and conventional morality, and were criticised by other anarchists as selfish and ineffective.
scope: The French and Italian illegalists of roughly 1880-1914: Clement Duval, Marius Jacob and his Travailleurs de la Nuit, Vittorio Pini, Ravachol and the Bonnot Gang. Based on Jacob's 1905 trial statement and secondary accounts. Excludes later anarchists who merely tolerated expropriation, and Jacob's 1948 doubts about illegalism.

keyFigures.name: Clement Duval
keyFigures.role: Often considered the founder of illegalism; defended individual reclamation at his 1887 trial.

keyFigures.name: Marius Jacob
keyFigures.role: Led the burglary band the Workers of the Night and gave the best-known statement of illegalist principles.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed; an anti-state individualist would not look to the state to provide care, and takes what it needs directly.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Jacob called wage work "the prostitution of work"; a reformist wage floor leaves the exploitation intact, though this is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Illegalists took wealth outside the market and saw it as rigged by owners; they did not champion markets, which is inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Hostile to the state in principle, and reclamation aimed at individuals' gain, not at handing industries to a state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Duval wanted direct expropriation for revolutionary action rather than state taxation; the issue is inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Illegalists criticised the focus on the working class and trade unions as a path to change.

property-fundamental.rationale: Jacob called individual property the most unjust of thefts and rejected morality that treats respect for it as a virtue.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reform by state regulation does not fit their rejection of state law; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Never addressed; they scorned state palliatives but not on dependency grounds.

worker-ownership.rationale: Individualist reclaimers rather than collectivists, yet Jacob wanted wealth shared; adherents split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Outlaws evading police and arrest had every reason to oppose surveillance; inferred from their constant clashes with police.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertine individualist milieu opposed state morality laws; the issue itself is not documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: They rejected the authority of courts and laws to judge anyone, and speech laws were used against anarchists.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchist rejection of rulers and obedience; Duval refused deference even to a police commissioner.

state-harmful.rationale: Jacob denied any right of courts to judge him and condemned the laws and institutions as serving the rich.

limit-guns.rationale: Jacob's band went armed and used weapons in self-defense; disarmament by law cuts against that.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from their view of police and army as enforcers of bourgeois order (s4); acts such as Duval stabbing an officer during his arrest are not a stated position on police funding or authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Individualists generally opposed state regulation of private conduct; inferred, not documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Prefer small autonomous groups to national power; inferred from gang and affinity organisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Jacob said repression only aggravates the evil, and prisons and penal colonies were brutal.

traditional-family.rationale: Hégot's 1903 letter rejected the Fatherland, Society and Morality, and illegalists scorned bourgeois morals.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Opposed to state marriage but favour freedom from morality laws; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Liberty over private bodily matters fits individualism; not documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: Jacob's band robbed priests and left graffiti mocking god; Jacob mocked promises of paradise.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern in the sources; no clear implication.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Hégot rejected the Fatherland and its morality as constraints on the individual.

gradual-change.rationale: Illegalists wanted to provoke revolt immediately and had grown tired of waiting.

reduce-immigration.rationale: They disdained the Fatherland and ran cross-border networks; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposed to every state-like authority, international ones included; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; they stood outside both capitalism's rules and its defenders.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rejects state military power; not addressed directly.

open-borders.rationale: Scorned the Fatherland and operated across borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: The sources never touch environmental limits, and nothing in their principles points either way.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Would not look to government programs; anachronistic.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not a theme in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Illegalists saw their acts as revolution itself, and Jacob said "I made my revolution".

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-authoritarian rejection of rule by any elite; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: State direction contradicts their individualist, anti-state stance.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; individualists and collectivists differed.

land-value-tax.rationale: A state tax reform is not their approach; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: They sought direct seizure rather than state taxation; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: State-provided stipend is not their method; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Anti-state; Duval did not want property merely to change hands to another owner.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They rejected individual property, though a diffuse-property picture is not directly addressed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Jacob objected to wage work as exploitation and foresaw wealth belonging to everyone, though they lived by taking money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; anarchist anti-state vs pro-market framing do not fit.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are the opposite of illegalist outlawry.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia notes anarchists opposed the state itself as the institution legitimising domination, and illegalists rejected waiting on organised mass movements, so a ruling party has no place.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Monarchy is not discussed, but the sources describe illegalists as anarchists opposed to the state and every form of unjust domination.

democracy-best.rationale: Jacob scorned "your institutions" and denied anyone's right to judge him, rejecting parliamentary order.

workers-councils.rationale: Illegalists distanced themselves from class-based mass organisation; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inference from their individualist anti-state outlook (s1): withdrawing from any authority is welcome, but regional secession from a country is not something the sources discuss.

political-violence-never.rationale: They practised propaganda of the deed, bombings and armed robbery.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rejected the fatherland and its institutions; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anticlerical; they would abolish both rather than separate them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Imrie reports Jacob's band robbed priests as 'social parasites' and mocked God at Tours cathedral, while Jacob's trial speech scorned the very laws he was judged by.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They denied any court's right to judge; private ones are not endorsed either.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejected the nation and its morality.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Jacob described a war between rich and poor, though illegalists were individualists.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Jacob wanted wealth shared, but the individualists were not egalitarian planners.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed by the illegalists; their hostility to property and states does not settle who should hold land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and state-to-state transfers are not something they argued about.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hostile to nation and state building.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hégot sought individual well-being by any means, and critics called them selfish.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental value questions do not appear in illegalist writing, so no position can be inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by Jacob, Duval or the gangs, and adherents had no common line on it.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The illegalists attacked the bourgeois order, not industry as such; no position is documented.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological change is absent from their writings, and nothing in their principles favours either side.

human-enhancement.rationale: Individual freedom of the body; inferred and anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Those evading police would want to hide from the state; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolt against existing order, not nostalgia.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They were practical about outcomes yet fiercely principled about rejecting law; adherents would not give a clear side.

direct-action.rationale: Their whole practice: theft, arson and bombing instead of ballots.

means-match-ends.rationale: Duval defended terror and theft as means, not as prefiguring the future society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not an illegalist theme; they lived in cities by burglary and sought comfort, not a return to the land.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The sources discuss wage exploitation but never the division of labor itself.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Jacob said all would belong to everyone, defending theft as the need to satisfy appetites.

production-for-use.rationale: Jacob criticised a system where producers have least; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Jacob said the more a man works the less he earns and called landlords the worst thieves.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and not tied to the working class as a ruling class.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Illegalists attacked capitalism's injustice but did not theorise imperialism or great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: They held that the rich are the real thieves and the state serves them; taxation per se not addressed.

harm-principle.rationale: Rejected the state's right to judge at all, so they would not grant it a harm-based mandate.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualists, but not framed in rights language.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Rejected voting but not framed in these terms.

positive-liberty.rationale: Jacob said society offered him only work, begging or theft, tying liberty to material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; they saw capital and the state as power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Hostile to nationalist ideology; not addressed.

total-state.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist opposition to the state described in s1, which concerns anarchists in general rather than anything an illegalist wrote.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rejecting the Fatherland and all states, they had no interest in national expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oaths of personal loyalty to lords are the kind of hierarchy anarchists reject as rule over the individual.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not discussed; Jacob's refusal to be a 'docile and worn out worker' creating wealth for others clearly implies rejecting labor bound to an owner.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological claim the sources never take up; adherents are not committed either way.

universal-morality.rationale: Jacob rejected conventional morality that treats property as virtue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: They left wage work rather than reform it, so democratic control of firms was not their concern.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State fiscal policy was outside their interests and is not discussed in the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: They wanted freedom from state and property alike but never argued about economic freedom as a condition of political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Any government, even one resting on moral example, is still rule over individuals, which they rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-religious, but not committed to rationalism as such.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Jacob condemned wage work as exploitation, and illegalists refused to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Jacob told the court that those who produce everything have nothing, which can only produce antagonism between the laboring and the owning class, and he 'made war on the rich'.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; they scorned the existing order but nothing documents a view on cultural institutions.

workers-nation.rationale: They criticised class-based organisation and rejected the Fatherland, so national working-class organising fits neither.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reject bourgeois morals and the law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: State law of this kind is anathema.

state-class-instrument.rationale: They saw state law as class justice favouring the bourgeoisie.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not a topic in the sources and is anachronistic for them.

national-mission.rationale: Hégot's rejection of the Fatherland rules out a national mission to export a form of government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Duval said "the thieves are the rich" and illegalists saw rulers as parasites.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Property protection by the state is just what they attacked.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Jacob claimed the right to live for all; but they rejected law, so inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Debates among state socialists about building socialism were not illegalist concerns.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed; they rejected states generally rather than analysing settler ones.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A state ban grounded in religious morality is the sort of law illegalists said an anarchist ignores.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strongly anticlerical, they would keep religious teaching away from children, though they opposed state schooling too.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of the state that illegalists shared (s1); the sources do not discuss the doctrine of a socialist state strengthening under encirclement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him, so authority needs the individual's consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; expelling a minority by state coercion is clearly contrary to anarchist opposition to the state and domination.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They initiated force by theft, arson and bombings and justified it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Egoist strands emphasised struggle but not documented.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anarchists were themselves repressed under such laws.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Jacob prized his liberty, independence and dignity as a man.

vanguard-party.rationale: Illegalists did not seek a party leading the masses.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Jacob justified theft from the rich on behalf of the exploited.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy never appears in the sources; the question is a state-programme one outside their concerns.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Jacob blamed social structure for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not discussed; they disdained national cohesion as a value, so would not endorse the premise.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: They rejected public office altogether, so choosing office-holders by lot was not an issue for them.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Illegalists were victims of emergency laws.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from their individualist anti-state outlook and their own illegal press (s1); the sources do not discuss media control as such.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party-controlled army is a tool of rule, and they opposed armies and rulers alike.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hostile to borders and citizenship regimes, they would see waiting periods as pointless state gatekeeping.

church-by-bishops.rationale: They robbed priests and mocked religion, so they would reject episcopal power over anyone.

clerical-rule.rationale: Imrie reports Jacob's band classed priests among the 'social parasites' they robbed and left 'All-powerful god, find your thieves!' at Tours cathedral.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Some illegalists were convicted of offences against public morals and scorned morality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They rejected presidents and rulers in the first place, so rules on their tenure were beside the point.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Jacob condemned landlords but individual property is rejected too.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; they were largely urban gang members.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not a theme in the sources, and no illegalist position is documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not discussed; their stance on the Fatherland does not settle a claim about cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Duval was sentenced to death and urged comrades to die rather than reach a penal colony.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Schooling policy is not discussed; they opposed both state schooling and morality laws, so they were split in effect.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anticlerical outlook leaves no room for scripture-based teaching in state schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Convictions for public morals offences; opposed morality law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship is a state category they rejected, along with the Fatherland and nationality.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is a state matter not addressed in the sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; they wanted freedom from all law rather than special exemptions for believers.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Property system is the problem; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Curtailing liberties for state development runs against their demand for personal independence.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is anachronistic, and they opposed state armament in any form.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rejected individual property outright rather than conditioning it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; regulatory environmental principles do not appear in their writing.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances between states are statist and militarist, which anarchists opposed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Questions of international law over annexation are not discussed by the illegalists.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Using military force to hold a state together contradicts their anti-state, anti-military stance.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Constitutional arrangements for regions were not a topic for them.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the illegalists' anarchist rejection of rulers and their anticlericalism (s1); the sources do not discuss sacred rulers.

character-from-environment.rationale: Jacob said society left him work, begging or theft.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in any source.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from their anarchist rejection of authority (s1); the sources do not discuss leader cults.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy does not appear in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate among state socialists that illegalists did not take part in.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on nationality rely on the Fatherland, which Hégot and other illegalists rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from their anticlericalism and demand for individual liberty (s3); the sources do not discuss apostasy laws.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed; the illegalists rejected both law and religious morality, so a religious dress law is clearly contrary to their principles.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is a state project that they did not discuss; their stance is inferred as hostile.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political union on ancestry is a nationalist project they would not support.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; minority self-government within a state is a state arrangement they did not address.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed by the illegalists, who were not working on minority emancipation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist theory of history that illegalists did not take up or reject in the sources.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is state regulation of the economy, and not something they campaigned for.

no-bailouts.rationale: Hostile to state aid to the rich; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They rejected both courts and majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs of states are statist and nationalist, which they opposed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding treaty standards are state instruments not in their field of concern.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; they were not building an alternative society's work ethic.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Illegalists held revolution should be provoked now by acts, not awaited from mass movement.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: They rejected hierarchy and privilege of birth, as anarchists do, though the sources do not state it directly.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by one society over another is rule they opposed on anarchist principles.

patriotic-education.rationale: Imrie quotes the illegalist press: 'We have had enough of always sacrificing ourselves for something. The Fatherland, Society and Morality have fallen.'

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policy is anachronistic and not covered by the sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: A public monetary body is a state institution; they were hostile to the state but did not discuss money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism avoids a general collapse is a Marxist debate they did not enter.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Seeking influence over former imperial territory is state power politics they rejected.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategy that is not found in illegalist sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist and anti-imperialist thesis not discussed in illegalist writing.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not discussed; they cared about their own freedom from law, not about owners' rights over others.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the treaties are a matter between states.

minority-veto.rationale: Individualist anarchism, which the illegalists came from, holds that no collective may bind an individual without consent, and Jacob denied any court's right to judge him (s2); this is implied by principle rather than stated as a rule for group decisions.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though some individualist anarchists were vegetarian.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in the sources consulted.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Jacob rejected philanthropy as a rich man's virtue; the rich were thieves.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred; they saw law and state as class instruments.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office to natives rests on the nation and on public offices, both of which they rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal question among communist parties that is not an illegalist concern.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; development strategy for poor countries was not an illegalist topic.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory back is a nationalist programme in tension with the rejection of the Fatherland.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; they rejected rule by anyone rather than choosing which group should lead.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Jacob stayed anti-fascist to the end; constitutions are not their frame.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A twentieth-century debate beyond the illegalists' period; sources give no position.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute about American history that is irrelevant to the illegalists' sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed, and national monuments would hold little value for people who rejected the Fatherland, so adherents are neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy debates are anachronistic and not covered by the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not covered by the illegalist sources and anachronistic.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: A question about different civilizations' political forms that the illegalists did not address.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for armies is a form of state power they strongly opposed.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and unpaid care labour was not an illegalist theme.

office-by-exam.rationale: They rejected holding public office at all, so how posts are filled was beside the point.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State protection of industries is a statist policy, so they would not endorse it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Occupancy-and-use tenure fits some individualist anarchists but is not documented for illegalists, and adherents are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination doctrine is anachronistic and not covered by the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Illegalists were charged with hedonism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State sponsorship of insurgents is state power politics, which they rejected, though they favoured armed revolt itself.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Armies sent to hold an alliance together are an instrument of state domination they opposed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: they see the state as the bourgeoisie's tool, so business capture of government is expected.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state altogether; they would not want the state to screen anything.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: they reject the state, the nation and family duty, so state incentives to breed are refused.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: they reject property and any authority that would limit who may take or hold it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Jacob called wage work the prostitution of work; state-provided jobs would still be wage labor.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: they reject all states and so any claim that states spread peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him and held that an anarchist need not take the law into account.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state: every state is an illegitimate power, so each should be left alone by others, though they do not state this.

industrial-unions.rationale: Illegalists criticised trade unions as a path to change; industrial form is not discussed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: they explain exploitation by property and the state, not a hidden minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of conventional morality and the state's authority over private life.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; they reject the state and its records alike.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; they took wealth outside the market without stating a view on supply chains.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gangs like Jacob's Travailleurs de la Nuit were small groups of trusted comrades, and they rejected permanent unions and federations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject all law, national and international alike, so the ranking question has no answer.

religious-nation.rationale: Illegalists rejected religion along with the state and conventional morality.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Illegalists reject the state, law and authority altogether, so ritual submission to any power is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from their individualist rejection of states and territorial claims; revenue sharing between regions is not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: They reject property as such and reclaim goods individually; collective ownership of the means of production is not their programme.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose all authority including authoritarian communism, but did not campaign to defeat communists.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state and of publicly funded institutions; not addressed directly.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from their atheism and rejection of conventional morality; the source on their religious views was not read in detail.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Jacob's trial statement denounces the capitalist order as organised theft that exploits workers, not as a stage toward something better.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; no single illegalist position on women's equality or its causes is documented in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from their individualism and hostility to public institutions; not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from their hostility to nation and state; the nation is a construct they reject, so state language policy would be rejected.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state authority and law; treaties with internal nations are not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They put the individual first and reject binding collective structures, though some founded free communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of nation and state; state-steered settlement to bind regions to a nation is the opposite of their outlook.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of both capitalist property and state authority, which rules out capitalism and authoritarian communism alike.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the illegalists' rejection of the state and of property, which leaves no basis for a people's superior claim to land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Never addressed and anachronistic; inferred from anarchist hostility to authoritarian and racist movements.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their rejection of state law and conventional morality, which makes criminalising private conduct unacceptable.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and all its repression, and were themselves hunted as an organised opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: They rejected law, church and conventional morality, so state punishment of religious dissent has no place in their outlook.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their opposition to the state and to exploitation by the ruling class.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; inferred from their rejection of binding collective duties and of religion, though they favoured armed revolt against states.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: They wanted every ruler removed, not only irreligious ones; the religious-law test is foreign to them, inferred from their atheistic anti-state stance.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Individualists distrusted collective decision-making as another authority, yet favoured people running their own lives; inferred and split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; their focus was individual revolt against property and law rather than a theory of overlapping oppressions, inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; they rejected state recognition in general but also conventional sexual morality, so the answer is inferred and neutral.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their insistence that individuals control their own lives and bodies against law and morality.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; they stood outside the left-right frame as individualist anarchists, but did not argue for combining the two.

alienated-labor.rationale: Jacob called wage work "the prostitution of work" and refused it, which matches the idea that waged labor estranges people from their own activity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their hostility to nationalism and to prejudice dressed up as morality.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They were atheists who denied any authority above the individual, whether God, state or law.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; they rejected both the state and religion, so neither side of this dispute is theirs.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; they took no interest in reforming employment law through the state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of both the state and property; a regulated market is a compromise they scorned.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from their anti-state anti-militarism, though they themselves practised armed violence.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of an economic order in which some are privileged; they took wealth immediately instead of waiting.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state and its wars; not addressed directly.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and all inherited authority and privilege, so hereditary rule is the opposite of their outlook (inferred from their anti-state stance).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; mutual banking is an anarchist idea, but illegalists took wealth directly rather than reforming credit, and this is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Illegalists never discussed international lenders; they opposed the state and its debts but did not campaign for governments to do anything, so no clear answer can be inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and its law and held that property was theft, so a franchise tied to property is the opposite of their view.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Individualist illegalists did not theorise this link and some were hostile to feminism as a cause; no clear position is documented.

reification.rationale: Jacob called wage work degrading and exploitative, which fits the idea that economic relations dominate people, though he did not use this vocabulary (inferred).

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Jacob's trial statement attacked the rich as owners of society's means, which suggests agreement, but press and assembly were not a topic of his and this is inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Illegalists rejected state law and judges outright, denying anyone's right to judge them, so a government by standing laws is not something they would endorse (inferred from Jacob's trial statement).

racial-franchise.rationale: They rejected nation, state and any franchise, and Jacob's band was international in outlook; racial restriction contradicts their anarchist principles.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the period; they rejected representative politics and a vote of any kind, so no clear answer can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; illegalists worked in secrecy and rejected the state, so they would not look to state transparency, but would not oppose it either (inferred).

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: They rejected religion and the legal control of private life, so a law restricting marriage by faith is contrary to their views.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: They rejected nationalism and prejudice and aimed at the rich, not at minorities, so targeting shops by religion contradicts their outlook (inferred).

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; illegalists rejected the state and all authority over the individual, so a lot-chosen body whose conclusions bind others would still be rule, though this is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed directly; illegalists rejected religion outright as part of the morality they scorned, so updating doctrine would hold little interest. Inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Jacob and Duval held that the rich had stolen their wealth from labor, so concentrated property is seen as a mark of domination; inferred, not argued as a liberty thesis.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Illegalists rejected conventional morality and authority, so a ban on sexual minorities would be rejected; the issue itself is not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Illegalists opposed religion but also rejected the state, so state-led indoctrination in any direction would be refused; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Jacob's trial statement and Duval's reclamation theory deny the legitimacy of law and the courts, and illegalists rejected the state outright, so policing and prison have no standing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Illegalists rejected government and majority and minority claims alike; guaranteed communal shares of executive power are inferred to be rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Illegalists took what they needed directly and scorned charity as a sop; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Illegalists rejected all office and rulers, so limiting terms in office accepts a legitimacy they denied; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Illegalists rejected voting and representation altogether, so delegated voting is inferred to be rejected as another form of government.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Never addressed; the individualist focus on one's own life and immediate revolt implies no support for long-term collective policy priorities.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Illegalists rejected religious and conventional authority, so exclusion of women from religious office would carry no weight; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Illegalists rejected authority and hierarchy, so a husband's final authority is inferred to be rejected; marriage is not directly discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and voting alike, so a franchise for residents is not their question; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: they rejected state law and regulation of property in favour of seizing what they needed, so legal caps are not their remedy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of property and law; the sources do not discuss patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state, conventional morality and discipline in service of any nation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state and its armed force; the sources do not discuss nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of states and armies; the sources do not discuss bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: They rejected state authority, so official recognition by governments is not their practice; the sources are silent.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Jacob's trial statement attacks the idle rich who live off the labour of others and defends living by one's own efforts, though by theft.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: They defended violence against the bourgeoisie as legitimate revolt, though Jacob's band tried to avoid killing; they would not renounce lethal force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: They rejected the state and nationalism, and anarchists generally see nations as recent constructs; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from their individualism, which rejects collective identity as a basis for politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: They rejected patriotism and the state, so veneration of the nation's dead is contrary to their outlook.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: They were materialist individualists who rejected conventional morality and religion.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of nation and homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: They opposed the state altogether, and the sources do not discuss cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Atheist and anti-religious, so the question is not theirs; the sources do not discuss it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Atheist and anti-religious, so the test in the statement is not theirs; the sources do not discuss it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: They rejected the nation and the state, so ethnic ownership of economic life is contrary to their principles.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: They rejected the state and its territorial administration; the sources are silent.

independent-unions.rationale: Illegalists scorned wage labour and union organisation alike, so the statement is mostly irrelevant to them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; illegalists rejected both the state and wage labour and did not debate what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state and its institutions, which they would not want to keep in public hands.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from illegalists' rejection of the state, law and parliaments of any form.

municipal-property.rationale: Illegalists rejected property in general and took what they needed individually, not for local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from their individualist rejection of organised authority and delegates, even coordinating ones.

family-wage.rationale: Jacob and others rejected wage labour itself and lived by reclaiming what they needed, so a wage standard is not a goal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from individualist stress on personal choice over bodily risk; regulators are state bodies they reject.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of state spending and taxation.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: clandestine people living outside the law would want money beyond state tracing.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: illegalists lived under false names and clandestine networks and would favour anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualist anarchism puts the individual above state and community; Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Jacob rejected conventional morality and religion; no spiritual programme is recorded.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of all state authority; they would not endorse a national parliament as final authority.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the illegalist writers or their accounts.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the illegalist writers or their accounts.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from their individualism and rejection of collective identities and nations.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from their individualism and anarchist rejection of nationalism and collective identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from anarchist antimilitarism: they rejected state armies and wars, leaving at most defensive force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Illegalists were individualists who rejected nations and borders; nothing in the sources ties a people to a nation by language, inferred from this.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates presuppose voting and state-recognised communities, both of which an anti-state, anti-religious individualist rejects; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Illegalists saw all states as oppressors of their own people rather than victims of foreign plots; inferred from their anti-state stance.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; they rejected both state provision and wage-earning, so tuition policy is not something they argued over.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Taxes are state levies that illegalists rejected as theft, and environmental policy was not addressed; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; their stress on living freely now and individual revolt gives no clear duty to the unborn, so adherents are not clearly one way.

women-distinct-values.rationale: As individualists they rejected group-based claims about distinct values; some illegalist women acted on equal terms, inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anti-militarism was common among anarchists, but illegalists wanted the state abolished rather than bargaining over arms levels; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Hostility to state secrecy and diplomacy follows from their rejection of government; they would prefer no treaties at all, so only mild agreement is inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: State controls on capital would give the state more power over property; illegalists wanted to seize wealth directly, inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and its law and lived by armed burglary and expropriation, so they would never accept a state monopoly on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from general anarchist anti-militarism and rejection of state authority; illegalist sources do not discuss it directly.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Illegalists rejected wage labor altogether and saw organised unionism as accommodation, so they opposed bargaining over wages within the system.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from total rejection of the state and of wage labor; a state top-up of wages would be rejected.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the state is rejected entirely, so legal limits on it are beside the point.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and the legal order; no interest in reforming international rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Illegalists wanted to destroy the state and its laws, not to capture them; this is central to the current.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the individualist-anarchist rejection of fixed systems; individuals chose how to live, though no blueprint for communities was set out.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to property and markets, which rules out treating nature as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Jacob and other illegalists rejected nation, state and conventional morality as tools of the bourgeoisie.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; they were hostile to the state and to debt but would not look to the state for relief.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; illegalists thought in terms of class and individual revolt, not regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the individualist rejection of fixed moral and social norms; a settled human nature grounding rights is doubtful for them.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state institutions; public media funded by the state would be rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the illegalists' rejection of conventional morality and religion; Jacob's trial statement offers no religious claims.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from illegalist hostility to the state; it would not look to state price guarantees or public purchase.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from anti-state and anti-militarist anarchism; illegalists reject state power and arms of every kind.

workers-own-party.rationale: Illegalists rejected parties, politics and wage labor, favouring individual revolt over any workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state law as such; as individualists they would also reject coercion over bodies, so the answer is mildly negative.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Illegalists rejected legal property and law, so a legal right to own and inherit land is not something they sought.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; nothing in illegalist sources bears on language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Illegalists rejected courts and property law, so liability regimes enforced by judges would not be sought.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the total rejection of authority; Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from illegalist insistence on individual freedom against every constraint.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Illegalists rejected law and punishment as instruments of bourgeois order, so fixed sentences would be abhorrent.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the state and its requirements, including state-imposed conditions on newcomers.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of wage labor and of compulsion generally; illegalists also dismissed unions as reformist, though the issue is not discussed.

voter-id.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and elections; identity checks would be state control they evade, though voting rules are never discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from their anti-state and anti-clerical rejection of law and conventional morality, which excludes legal privilege for any church.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Illegalists rejected elections and rulers altogether, so they would not accept electoral selection as making a government legitimate; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: They rejected conventional morality and many adopted free-love individualism; inferred from that, as sexual conduct is not the sources' focus.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from their absolute hostility to state power over individuals.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state and their preference for taking what they need directly rather than receiving state payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anarchists rejected voting and office for everyone, so a right to vote and hold office is not something they sought; no direction is inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from their anti-clerical rejection of religion and conventional morality; women's oppression specifically is not discussed.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of social hierarchy and categories imposed by the bourgeois order; not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of the state; they would not look to government ministries to deliver equality.

missingStatements.text: Theft from the wealthy is justified when it is done to meet one's own needs or to fund a cause.
missingStatements.rationale: Individual reclamation is the defining illegalist practice, defended by Duval and Jacob as taking back what the rich had stolen.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow tactic of one ideology; initiating-force-wrong and taxation-theft already cover property-violation questions.

missingStatements.text: A person has no duty to obey laws that they have not personally agreed to.
missingStatements.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him and Antoine wrote that an anarchist need not take the law into account.

notes: Illegalism is a tactic as much as a doctrine; most answers on issues the illegalists never discussed are low-confidence inferences from their anti-state, anti-property individualism. Jacob's gang gave a share to propaganda, while some members refused on individualist grounds.
